text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-98321) — high TLS handshake failures observed at edge-eu-west-1, 5xx spike on /api/generate. Alerting policy: network.lb.tls.handshake > 15m. Link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/98321 :rotating_light:

maya: acked. I'm oncall for infra, will take first look.

pd-bot: Incident acknowledged by maya (oncall). Escalation policy: notify nate after 5m if not resolved.

nate: seeing the same in our dashboards — TLS errors are concentrated in eu-west-1, but a subset of requests are returning successful. Could be a regional cert mismatch or an SNI issue with the new edge routing.

ross: any recent push to edge-proxy configs? I did a config rollout at 03:10UTC but only to canary pool, not full.

maya: checking deploys now. No full rollout in last 24h. Canary rollout logs show one listener change to prefer http2/alpn order.

carla: customer-reports: two enterprise customers reported failed generator calls from EU while US works. They see 502/523.

maya: running quick curl from eu vm ->
```
$ curl -v https://api.prod.redwood.example.eu/api/generate -H 'Host: api.prod.redwood.example'
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate is OK
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello
* SSL peer certificate was not OK: certificate has expired
* Closing connection 0
```

nate: that looks like a cert error on the edge host side. Checking cert rotation logs for eu.

ross: I see a failed cert rotation job at 02:58UTC for region eu-west-1: ACME rate-limited, fallback certificate was deployed. Fallback cert appears to be from a different CN (internal-edge.example) which doesn't match SNI, leading to client cert mismatch.

maya: that matches the mixed success — some requests routed to old hosts with valid certs, others to fallback with wrong CN. Impact: partial region outage, ~30% qps failing with TLS handshake.

carla: flagging impacted customers: acme-biz, ledgerly, and two more on EU tenancy. I'm preparing a customer update template.

oncall-eu: hey — handing off to me for longer remediation, I'm on EU escalation.

pd-bot: Handoff: maya -> oncall-eu at 03:22UTC. Notified nate and ross.

nate: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic away from eu-west-1 using weight adjustment to dark-edge-1 -> dark-edge-2; 2) roll back the fallback cert to previous valid cert; 3) re-run cert rotation with manual ACME throttle handling.

maya: executing weight shift now. Using traffic-control tool:
```
$ trafficctl set-weight --region eu-west-1 --pool edge-canary --weight 0.1
$ trafficctl set-weight --region eu-west-1 --pool edge-stable --weight 0.9
```

maya: weight shift started — monitoring. Metrics: TLS handshakes failing decreasing on canary but still some errors.

ross: I'm initiating cert rollback. Found previous cert bundle at s3://redwood-secrets/edge-eu/certs/bundle-2026-02-10.pem

ross: rolling cert back to bundle-2026-02-10 on 4 instances (edge-a,b,c,d) via runbook step:
```
$ ansible-playbook -i inventory/eu edge-deploy.yml --extra-vars 'cert_bundle=bundle-2026-02-10.pem'
```

nate: quick check against target groups: AWS reports several targets in the eu target-group as Unhealthy with reason TLS error.
```
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu:tg/abcd
TARGET: i-0abcd   State: unhealthy  Reason: TLS handshake failed
```

oncall-eu: while we roll back, we should also increase connection timeout on proxy to avoid noisy terminations for in-flight requests. I'll apply a 30s increase.

maya: applied connection-timeout patch to listeners. Hoping to reduce 5xx noise.

carla: draft customer message ready — will send once we have a clear mitigation timeline.

pd-bot: PagerDuty note: Incident acknowledged, oncall-eu now owner. If resolution not achieved in 30m, auto-escalate to SRE manager.

ross: rollback succeeded on edge-a,b. Edge-c,d still finishing — rebalancing in flight.

maya: checks: curl -> certificate now OK on edge-a,b. Handshake errors down from 30% -> 6% in the last 5m.

nate: good. Continue rollback on remaining instances. After rollback completes, we'll trigger a controlled cert rotation with increased ACME backoff and validation.

oncall-eu: I'll keep the traffic weight conservative until we confirm stable for 15m. We'll keep an incident update cadence every 10m.

carla: sending customer advisory now with remediation steps and ETA.

maya: monitoring for a full minute window: no new TLS handshake increases. 5xx rate trending to baseline.

pd-bot: Resolution checklist: verify all targets healthy, confirm cert rotation queued with manual mode, close PD incident after postmortem created.

ross: opened incident doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/98321 — added timeline and RCA notes.

nate: post-incident actions: (1) add ACME backoff and alert on rotation failures, (2) add canary validation step that verifies CN matches SNI before promoted, (3) runbook update for trafficctl weight steps.

oncall-eu: agreed. I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates.

maya: switching to monitoring-only, thank you all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident PD-98321 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Auto-close will not happen; manual close after postmortem.

carla: marking customers notified.

maya: last note — follow up to schedule a dry-run for cert rotation in staging to exercise ACME limits and fallback behavior.

oncall-eu: ack. I'll put it on the infra backlog and ping schedulers.

carla: thanks team.

(End of thread)
